references.text: Earlier in the chapter, cities of refuge are established for someone who kills another by accident, without intent—the same principle described in verse 23.
The preceding verse describes a similar situation where someone is pushed without hostility, which parallels the description of unintentional killing.
Deuteronomy gives a similar example of unintentional killing where there was no prior enmity and describes the right to refuge.
Contrasts with intentional murder where there was hatred and hostility, which is the opposite of the situation described in Numbers 35:23.
Joshua repeats the laws concerning cities of refuge for someone who kills another unintentionally and without intent.
The basis for a place of refuge for one who did not plan the killing but where God allowed it to happen.
David shows that he did not seek harm against Saul, similar to the expression 'did not seek his misfortune' in Numbers 35:23.
